precepts.text: Before Zerubbabel the great mountain, Babylon, becomes a plain, and he shall bring forth the headstone with shoutings of grace, grace unto it; Zerubbabel brings forth the headstone, and Zerubbabel is of Solomon's line.
precepts.point: Behold, I will bring forth my servant the Branch, and the stone laid before Joshua with seven eyes; the Branch and the stone are Christ.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

precepts.why:
“for, behold, I will bring forth my servant the BRANCH.” Who is that? Christ. And the next chapter says who brings him forth: “Who art thou, O great mountain? before Zerubbabel thou shalt become a plain.” The great mountain is Babylon, made a plain, destroyed.

“and he shall bring forth the headstone thereof with shoutings, crying, Grace, grace unto it.” Who shall bring forth the headstone? Zerubbabel. Chapter 3 said the Lord will bring forth his servant the Branch; here Zerubbabel brings forth the headstone, which is the same as the Branch. And the headstone brings grace unto us.

How will Zerubbabel bring him forth? Through his line. And Zerubbabel comes out of Solomon's line. Matthew 1 shows it: “And after they were brought to Babylon, Jechonias begat Salathiel; and Salathiel begat Zorobabel”, born in Babylon, and from Zorobabel down to “Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ.” Joseph comes out of the line of kings, the kingdom of Solomon, heir to the throne, but in captivity, with Rome calling the shots and an Edomite, Herod, on the throne, until Christ returns and conquers Edom. There is no scripture that says Jeconiah's line was cursed from being kings; that doctrine was made to justify a virgin birth. The Zerubbabel of Luke 3 is a different one, of Nathan's line: Joseph is written there because he inherited Heli's inheritance as his son-in-law, Heli being Mary's father with no sons.

precepts.text: The stone which the builders refused is become the head stone of the corner; the headstone Zerubbabel brings forth is the same stone laid before Joshua.
precepts.point: Behold, I will bring forth my servant the Branch, and the stone laid before Joshua with seven eyes; the Branch and the stone are Christ.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

precepts.why:
Zechariah says, “For behold the stone that I have laid before Joshua; upon one stone shall be seven eyes.” The Branch and the stone are Christ. Then Zerubbabel “shall bring forth the headstone thereof.”

What is the headstone? “The stone which the builders refused is become the head stone of the corner.” Who is the Branch, who is the stone? It's the same thing. The headstone Zerubbabel brings forth is the same stone laid before Joshua, and the same servant the Branch the Lord said he would bring forth: Christ, refused by the builders and made the head of the corner.

So when the Lord says “I will remove the iniquity of that land in one day”, he is going into Christ. The stone laid before Joshua the high priest and his fellows, men wondered at for a sign, is the Christ who would come through Zerubbabel's loins.

precepts.text: Built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Jesus Christ himself being the chief corner stone, in whom we grow into an holy temple; Zerubbabel laid the foundation of the second temple with a literal stone and brought forth through his loins the stone that builds the temple we are.
precepts.point: Behold, I will bring forth my servant the Branch, and the stone laid before Joshua with seven eyes; the Branch and the stone are Christ.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

precepts.why:
Zerubbabel built the second temple, so he brought forth a literal stone with a foundation. That's the first level. But it is twofold: he also brought forth the other stone through his loins, to build up the temple which is us here in the room.

“And are built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Jesus Christ himself being the chief corner stone”: the chief corner stone, the headstone. “In whom all the building fitly framed together groweth unto an holy temple in the Lord”: that's us. “In whom ye also are builded together for an habitation of God through the Spirit.”

So we are that holy temple that Christ builds. Zerubbabel laid the foundation of the second temple, and he brought forth the same stone and the same foundation, which is Christ, on whom we are built. Praise the Lord for that.

precepts.text: Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, that I will raise unto David a righteous Branch: talking about Christ. In his days Judah shall be saved, and Israel shall dwell safely: and this is his name whereby he shall be called, THE LORD OUR RIGHTEOUSNESS.
precepts.point: In that day shall ye call every man his neighbour under the vine and under the fig tree: that is in the kingdom.

note.label: We Are Born in Babylon

precepts.why:
In the Persian captivity there was Joshua the high priest, of the tribe of Levi, and Zerubbabel the governor, of the tribe of Judah. The Lord speaks to Joshua and his fellows, “for, behold, I will bring forth my servant the BRANCH.” The Branch is Christ, and Jeremiah 23 shows it.

“Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, that I will raise unto David a righteous Branch, and a King shall reign and prosper, and shall execute judgment and justice in the earth.” The righteous Branch raised unto David is Christ, the King who will reign and execute justice.

“In his days Judah shall be saved, and Israel shall dwell safely: and this is his name whereby he shall be called, THE LORD OUR RIGHTEOUSNESS.” That is the same day Zechariah speaks of. The stone laid before Joshua with its seven eyes, and those eyes are the angels. “I will remove the iniquity of that land in one day”: that is Christ dying on the cross. And “In that day”, every man shall call his neighbour “under the vine and under the fig tree”: that is in the kingdom, when Israel dwells safely under the Branch.

precepts.text: Behold the man whose name is The BRANCH; and he shall build the temple of the Lord: not the second temple; this is about the third and the fourth. He shall bear the glory, and shall sit and rule upon his throne; and he shall be a priest upon his throne: and the counsel of peace shall be between them both: going into the priesthood and the kingship, and Christ fulfilled both.
precepts.point: In that day shall ye call every man his neighbour under the vine and under the fig tree: that is in the kingdom.

note.label: We Are Born in Babylon

precepts.why:
The Branch appears again in Zechariah 6: “Behold the man whose name is The BRANCH; and he shall grow up out of his place, and he shall build the temple of the Lord.” That is not the second temple; it is about the third and the fourth.

“Even he shall build the temple of the Lord; and he shall bear the glory, and shall sit and rule upon his throne; and he shall be a priest upon his throne: and the counsel of peace shall be between them both.” Both is the priesthood and the kingship. He sits and rules on his throne as a king, and he is a priest on that same throne.

That is why Zechariah 3 speaks to Joshua the high priest, and why Zerubbabel the governor stands alongside him: the priest from Levi and the ruler from Judah. Christ fulfilled both offices, the priesthood and the kingship, in one man, the Branch.

precepts.text: The sceptre shall not depart from Judah: the kingship shall not depart from Judah; nor a lawgiver from between his feet: that is the priesthood, letting you know Christ would come from the rod; there is no immaculate anything, that is Egyptian and Babylonian make believe; until Shiloh come: that is the Messiah, Christ; and unto him shall the gathering of the people be.
precepts.point: In that day shall ye call every man his neighbour under the vine and under the fig tree: that is in the kingdom.

note.label: We Are Born in Babylon

precepts.why:
The priesthood and the kingship that Christ fulfilled go back to Jacob's blessing on Judah: “The sceptre shall not depart from Judah”: the kingship shall not depart from Judah. “nor a lawgiver from between his feet”: that is the priesthood, and what is between a man's feet is his rod. It shows Christ would come from the rod. There is no immaculate anything; that is make-believe, Egyptian and Babylonian fairy tales. “until Shiloh come”: that is the Messiah, Christ. “and unto him shall the gathering of the people be.”

Matthew 1 traces the line through the captivity. “And after they were brought to Babylon, Jechonias begat Salathiel; and Salathiel begat Zorobabel”, and so down to “Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ.” That is the Branch coming out of Zerubbabel, the governor who stood with Joshua the high priest.

In the sit-down with Captain Matathias and Captain Galiah, the dude with that stupid hat argued there was a curse on Jechonias that no one of his seed would sit as king, so the genealogy is ruled out. But after Babylon came in, that was it: Zedekiah was taken away and his sons were killed, and no king sat on the throne in Israel. There was no king in the time of Christ. When he came, the people loved him so much that they wanted to “take him by force, to make him a king”, and “he departed again into a mountain himself alone.” By the prophets, there would be no more king until Christ returns: the sceptre waits for Shiloh.

precepts.text: Let thy priests be clothed with righteousness; and let thy saints shout for joy.
precepts.point: The garment is twofold. The change of raiment is Israel becoming righteous: keeping the commandments, putting the Most High first, and dealing rightly with him and with our own people.

note.label: Zechariah 3: The Filthy Garments Taken Away

precepts.why:
The garment is twofold. Joshua's filthy garments are taken away and he is clothed with change of raiment, and that change of raiment is Israel becoming righteous. “Let thy priests be clothed with righteousness; and let thy saints shout for joy.”

The priests clothed with righteousness is the change of raiment: keeping the commandments, putting the Most High first, and dealing rightly with him and with our own people. When our iniquity passes from us, that is the garment we are clothed with.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 11 A Time Of Defamation

precepts.why: Clothed in sackcloth is referring to filthy garments. When we wore sackcloth we were in a state of mourning: we would put dust on our head and wipe it in our clothes, rip our clothes up, and wear sackcloth, burlap, the potato-sack fabric. “Now Joshua was clothed with filthy garments, and stood before the angel. And he answered and spake unto those that stood before him, saying, Take away the filthy garments from him. And unto him he said, Behold, I have caused thine iniquity to pass from thee, and I will clothe thee with change of raiment.” When Joshua had on these filthy garments, these dirty clothes, in Revelation that is going into the sackcloth. Why? We were still under the curses of God, but remember, he gave us power. So we are prophesying clothed in filthy garments, and the sackcloth represents iniquity, sin.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 11 A Time Of Defamation

precepts.why: Remember Joshua had on filthy garments; now watch what it says here. “Hear now, O Joshua the high priest, thou, and thy fellows that sit before thee: for they are men wondered at: for, behold, I will bring forth my servant the BRANCH.” The BRANCH is making reference to Christ. Joshua was the high priest, and chapter 4 goes into Zerubbabel. The two kingdoms are referenced the way Christ spoke with Moses and Elijah: Zechariah makes mention of Joshua and Zerubbabel.
